title: Check yourself: The loop: results, errors and stop reasons

questions.stem: A handler for a database lookup throws because the row does not exist. What should the loop do?

options.text: End the conversation and return the exception to the caller
options.says: Ruled out because the loop is to "continue the conversation forward with a `tool_result` that indicates the error", not to end it.

options.text: Send a result flagged as an error whose message says what to try
options.says: The page says "Write instructive error messages", with "what went wrong and what Claude should try next".

options.text: Return an empty string so the model reads the call as complete
options.says: Ruled out because "An exception that becomes an empty string tells the model the call worked."

options.text: Run the same call again until the row appears, without telling the model
options.says: Ruled out because the model must be told of the failure: "Claude will then incorporate this error into its response to the user."

questions.stem: The assistant turn holds two `tool_use` blocks. How does the next request carry the outputs?

options.text: Two user messages, one result in each, in the order of the calls
options.says: Ruled out because the trap is "Sending results one message at a time", and the rule is to "Return every result together in the next user message".

options.text: One assistant message in which both outputs are recorded as text
options.says: Ruled out because results are sent by the user: "a user message with the `tool_result` blocks".

options.text: One user message that opens with a sentence and then lists the results
options.says: Ruled out because a sentence before the first result "will cause a 400 error".

options.text: One user message with both results first and any text after them
options.says: The page says "In the user message containing tool results, the tool_result blocks must come FIRST in the content array."

origin.section: The formatting rules that cause 400 errors

questions.stem: A reply arrives with `stop_reason` of `pause_turn`. What does the page say to do?

options.text: Treat the reply as a refusal and stop the loop with that status
options.says: Ruled out because the table gives a refusal its own reaction: "status `refused`; the same request is not repeated".

options.text: Pass the assistant content back untouched, and call once more
options.says: The page says to send "the assistant response back as it is, keep the same `tools` array".

options.text: Run the missing tool and return its output in a `tool_result` block
options.says: Ruled out because a paused turn "is different from `tool_use`, which requires `tool_result` blocks".

options.text: Raise `max_tokens` and repeat the request that produced the pause
options.says: Ruled out because a raised limit belongs to a cut-off reply: "a cut-off `tool_use` block needs a higher `max_tokens`".
